title: Covered calls and short puts are a bet on implied vs realized volatility
summary: When you sell covered calls or cash-secured puts, you bet that implied volatility, which you collect on day one, is higher than realized volatility, which you pay in effect by expiry. Sell when implied is high and realized stays low. Focus on that relationship to find an edge.

params.label: Implied minus realized
params.help: Average gap between implied and realized volatility, in vol points.

steps.caption: The stock path during the life of the short option.
Implied volatility is what you are paid on day one.
Realized volatility is what you pay, in effect, by expiry.
When implied is well above realized, the seller has an edge.
When the stock tanks, realized jumps and the seller pays more than collected.

takeaways: Selling options is a bet that implied volatility exceeds realized volatility.
Sell when implied is high and realized is low.
A big drop or a big rally can cost more than the premium collected.
caveats: The clip refers to the speaker's yield metric; it is promotional and unverified.
